GRANT OF LAND UNDER CLAUSE (b) OF SUB
PARAGRAPH (1) OF PARAGRAPH (6) OF THE
LAND REFORMS (BALUCHISTAN PAT FEEDER CANAL) REGULATION, 1972, RULES, 1976
Grant of land under paragraph 6 (1) (b) of MLR‑117 Rules, 1976
[Gazette of Baluchistan,
Extraordinary, 31st August 1976]
No. 53‑CLR/2888.‑1n
exercise of the powers conferred by paragraph 19 of the Land Reforms (Baluchistan Pat Feeder Canal) Regulation, 1976,
the Government of Baluchistan is pleased to make the following Rules, namely :‑
1. Short title and
commencement.‑(i) These rules may be called the Grant of Land under
Clause (b) of Sub‑paragraph (1)
of Paragraph 6 of the Land Reforms (Baluchistan Pat Feeder Canal) Regulation,
1972, Rules, 1976.
(#) They shall come into force
at once.
2. Definitions.‑(1) In these
Rules, unless the context otherwise
requires, the following expressions shall have the meaning hereby respectively
assigned to them, that is to say :‑
(a) "Application"
means an application made for grant of land under the provisions of clause (b)
of sub‑paragraph (!) of paragraph 6 of the Regulation in pursuance of the
Notifications Nos. 52‑60 of 9th January 1975 and 272‑96 of 31st January 1975 issued by the Board
of Revenue, Baluchistan or deemed to have been made under subsection (a) of section 8 of the Land Reforms
(Baluchistan Pat Feeder Canal) (Amendment) Ordinanec, (976 (Baluchistan
Ordinance No, VII of 1976).
(b) "Collector" means Collector of the Nasirabad
District;
(c) "Grantee" means a person who has been
granted or deemded to have been granted land under these Rules;
(d) "Regulation" means the Land Reforms
(Baluchistan Pat Feeder Canal) Regulation, 1972.
(2) Words and expressions used but not defined in
these Rules shall have the same meaning as assigned to them in the Regulation.
3. Disposal of
applications.‑(1) After the receipt of the application, the Land
Reforms Officer shall fix a date for its hearing and also give an intimation of
that date, to the Collector to represent the Government.
(2) The land Reforms Officer shall, on the date fixed
for the purpose, or on the date to which such hearing may be adjourned, hear
the applicant
and the Collector or his nominee. Alter taking into
consideration all the evidence produced before him and after examining any
record or making such enquiry in such manner, as he may deem fit or necessary,
the Land Reforms Officer shall pass an order accepting or rejecting the
application.
(3) Where applications are made by different persons
in respect of the same land, the Land
Reforms Officer shall, as far as possible, consider the respective claims of all such applicants before passing
order.
(4) The applications shall be disposed of, as far as
possible, in an Ijlas‑e‑Aam and in or near the Mauza where the land
in question is situated, or at Tehsil or District headquarters.
(5) The Land Reforms Officer shall, as early as
possible after passing his order, supply certified copies thereof to the
persons who had made applica tions with respect to the land concerned.
(6) Whenever a part of a survey
number is granted to a person, a rough
sketch map of that survey number indicating roughly the
position of the land so granted shall be added in the order of the Land Reforms
Officer.
4. Applications
by minors etc.‑If any of the
applicants is a minor or of unsound
mind, or is a woman, he/she may be represented by a guardian, or the person who
has the care of that person, or by an authorised agent.
5. Appeal.‑(1)
Any person aggrieved by an order passed by the Land Reforms Officer may,
within 20 days of the passing of the order, prefer an appeal to the Board of Revenue.
(2) An appeal shall be preferred in the form of a memorandum and shall be
authenticated by the signatures of the applicant or his duly authorised
representative or agent.
(3) The memorandum shall be accompanied by a
certified copy of the order appealed
